title: Modeling the wet bulb globe temperature using standard meteorological measurements
authors: Liljegren JC, Carhart RA, Lawday P, Tschopp S, Sharp R
journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Hygiene
population: Outdoor WBGT model for U.S. Army chemical-munition depots, validated against WBGT measurements at all depots
findings: A model of outdoor WBGT using only standard meteorological data, with separate submodels of natural wet bulb and globe temperatures based on fundamental heat and mass transfer principles.
The model has no site-dependent parameters.
It achieves accuracy better than 1 C against WBGT measurements at all depots.
limitations: Occupational (military) validation at U.S. depots; the abstract does not list inputs (the usual inputs are air temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed and solar radiation, from background knowledge, not the abstract); not validated for running or non-U.S. races.
implications: Implement WBGT as the Liljegren physics-based model from hourly forecast air temperature, relative humidity, pressure, wind speed and solar radiation; expect about 1 C accuracy under ideal inputs, more with forecast error.
If solar radiation is unavailable, estimate from cloud cover and widen the stated uncertainty; never silently substitute air temperature for WBGT.
Keep it a pure function in shared/ with unit tests against published reference values (full text needed; not verified here).

verification.notes: Crossref (JOEH, online 2008-08, print 2008-09) and Europe PMC abstract re-fetched. Input list is not in the abstract; verify against the full text before implementing. Heat index (Steadman/Rothfusz) is not covered by any verified paper.
